claim: AVC available is a fund/cover-group level metric, not an FR-line-level metric. All FR lines on the same (FONDS, FUNDSCTR, CMMTITEM-rolled-to-control-object) draw from a single shared AVC pool. The pool is calculated as: Available = FMAVCT.allotment - sum(open FMIOI commitments) - sum(FMIFIIT actuals) on the same key. FMAVC005 fires when Available <= 0 + new posting amount > 0. The triggering FR line is incidental; the constraint is the fund pool.

Downstream filters reduce actual BCM batch creation: (1) PM must be DMEE-enabled (T042Z.XBKKT='X' — 100% clean cut: no XBKKT='' ever creates a BCM batch), (2) co code ICTP is structurally excluded (0/603 runs), (3) BCM grouping rules (IMG > FSCM > BCM > Payment Grouping > Rule Maintenance) evaluate and assign one of 14 UNESCO-custom RULE_IDs (UNES_AP_ST, UNES_TR_TR, PAYROLL, IIEP_AP_ST, UIS_AP_MAX, UBO_AP_MAX, UIL_AP_ST, UNES_AP_10/11/EX/IK, UNES_AR_BP, UBO_AP_ST, UIS_AP_ST). The observation 'LAUFI ending in B ↔ BCM batch' (100% correlation) is a SYMPTOM of UNESCO naming convention for BCM-destined F110 variants combined with the OBPM5 wildcard match, NOT a SAP routing rule. Supersedes legacy brain memory claim 'LAUFI prefix B=BCM, 0/T/M=Direct' (falsified: prefix-B runs have 0% BCM linkage; prefix-0 runs with suffix-B have 100%).

evidence_for.cite: BNK_BATCH_HEADER: 27,443 batches 2014-2026, 100% have LAUFI ending in B. REGUH (full schema extract 15mo, 505,636 rows, 9,163 distinct runs): XBKKT='' → 0/2,941 BCM (100% clean negative), XBKKT='X' → 1,045/6,222 BCM (16.8%). Co code ICTP: 0/603 BCM. Companies UNES/IIEP/UIL/UBO/UIS: 10-29% BCM within XBKKT='X'.

https://www.se80.co.uk/saptables/t/tfib/tfiblmpayblockid.htm — confirms TFIBLMPAYBLOCKID is 'Run Identification for Cross-Payment Run Payment Medium'. Tcode OBPM5 = 'Cross-Payment Run Payment Medium / Reservation for Cross-Payment Run Payment Media'.

claim: XSLT CGI_XML_CT_XSLT (SAP-std, devclass=ID-DMEE) is an identity transformation with EMPTY-ELEMENT REMOVAL. Template 1 matches '*[not(child::node())]' with empty body — deletes any leaf element with no children/text. Template 2 matches '*[string() or @*[string()]]' — copies elements with text content or attributes with values. EFFECT: V001 structured PstlAdr nodes that are empty (e.g., <BldgNb/> when vendor has no HOUSE_NUM1) are AUTOMATICALLY REMOVED from final XML before file write. They serve different purposes: (1) MULESOFT = automated budget loading at biennium-start, carries Workplan/Allocation context including FIPEX-aware Commitment_Item__c. (2) FB01 = manual real-posting reclassifications (mid-biennium adjustments, biennium-end revenue moves like A_BANSAL 257-doc batch). Implication for fix paths: FIX-A (MULESOFT FIPEX-aware) ONLY helps biennium-start budget loading. It has NO effect on FB01 reclassifications, which produce the actual model-gap defect at biennium-end. The 257 FB01s on 2026-01-31 are real postings - they bypass any MULESOFT enhancement. Therefore: FIX-A scope is narrow. FIX-E (pre-flight HARD-BLOCK on FB01/FMBB/FMBBT) is necessary. FIX-F (Meta-AVC) is the ONLY path that catches every change source (budget OR real, automated OR manual).

claim: Root config that PERMITS the FM-PS model gap (TIER_1 from fmavct_2026): UNESCO's AVC derivation rule FMAFMAP013500109 (env 9HZ00001) collapses 8 of the 9 operational FIPEX (11, 13, 20, 30, 40, 50, 10\' and REVENUE) into a SINGLE control object called TC. Only PSC (FIPEX 80) keeps its own separate control object. Therefore the AVC engine validates against only 2 buckets per fund (TC + 80) instead of the 9 FIPEX visible in FMIFIIT. The TC bucket includes REVENUE in its pool, so as long as REVENUE > sum(operational consumption), TC stays positive and AVC permits postings — even though individual operational FIPEX are deeply negative. AVC is structurally blind to per-FIPEX deficits because it never sees them. UNESCO-wide pattern: 6,550 control objects use TC aggregator out of ~9,500 FMAVCT_2026 rows = ~80% of fund-FundCenter combinations are vulnerable to this exact pattern. Two root-config fixes: FIX-G1 (modify FMAFMAP013500109 so each FIPEX has its own control object — granular AVC) or FIX-G2 (keep TC aggregation but exclude REVENUE from the pool). Either is ~1 sprint config + UAT — cheapest structural fix yet identified, alternative to FIX-E/F.

claim: INC-000008088 Treasury interest GL split is constrained by an architectural invariant: bank statements can only be re-routed to specific GLs when the bank emits a SPECIFIC external transaction code (e.g. NINT — Normal Interest) that distinguishes interest from other credits. Banks that emit only GENERIC codes (NTRF, NCHK, NCLR) for ALL credit lines — including interest — CANNOT be split because there is no signal in the MT940 to tell SAP which credit is interest versus a regular transfer. At UNESCO, only Societe Generale exposes NINT reliably; all other Treasury HQ banks (BNP-Paribas, CIC, CRCAM, Banque Populaire, Citibank, Standard Chartered, Northern Trust BFM/HED, etc.) use generic NTRF for interest credits. Therefore the final implementation of INC-8088 splits ONLY the SOG banks (Group A → 7044013 via existing INTEREST_REC mask redirect; Group B → 7044014 via NEW SOG_FRB + 111B + INTEREST_REC_B). Group C (ASHI/Nessim) and Group D (PFF) remain on 7044011 as a known limitation, accepted by Treasury (M. Spronk validated 2026-05-05). The original architectural plan (TR_TRNFA/B/C/D + SOG_FRA + 111A/B/C/D + INTEREST_REC_A/B/C/D — 4-way clone) is OBSOLETE.

claim: UNESCO's entire Gold DB extraction floor (24M+ rows, ~68 extracted tables) depends on a SINGLE function module -- RFC_READ_TABLE. As of 2026 this is SAP-tolerated and is the vendor-recommended compliant alternative to ODP-RFC (Theobald), so it is NOT restricted by Note 3255746. Residual risk is strategic/directional, not imminent: SAP is broadly moving to gatekeep third-party data access (Forrester 2026) and steer customers to SAP Business Data Cloud / ODP-OData. IF SAP ever extends restrictions to generic table-read RFC, the entire Gold DB refresh is the single point of failure. Mitigation: ODP-OData / Business Data Cloud (CDS/OData building blocks exist via sap_segw). Monitor; not urgent.

evidence_for.cite: Single point of dependency: every extract_*.py routes through the shared rfc_read_paginated() -> RFC_READ_TABLE. There is no second extraction mechanism feeding the Gold DB.

Note 3255746 formalizes SAP policy of blocking third-party direct data access (ODP first). RFC_READ_TABLE is the more exposed flank under the same governance philosophy and is documented by SAP as not released for productive use. Forward-looking inference, not a current restriction.

resolution_notes: Reframed Session #78 after web corroboration: earlier wording (RFC_READ_TABLE not released / the exposed flank) was an overstatement. Current consensus = table-read RFC is the recommended compliant path. Risk downgraded to strategic-direction watch item.

claim: The time-split (which project receives cost-recovery charges, in what proportion, for which months) is NOT derivable from SAP master data. claim: WBS PS-budget channel is GUI-only (CJ30/KBPP family) — no clean single-call RFC equivalent. KBPP_EXTERN_UPDATE raises DA300 NOT_FOUND without the full CJ30 buffer/profile context even with IMP_CHECK=X. Custom Y*BUDGET* FMs are readers/loggers only; BAPI_BUS2054_SET_STATUS = status only; BAPI_0050_CREATE = FM fund-center object (OBJNR FS*), NOT WBS (OBJNR PR*). WBS budgeting is a TWO-STEP process: (1) CJ30 sets the original/current budget → stored in BPJA as WRTTP=41 (current budget); (2) CJ32 releases it → stored in BPJA as WRTTP=42 (released budget). Budget is ANNUAL (table BPJA by GJAHR), NOT overall (BPGE WRTTP=01 was empty for WBS 650RER0008 / OBJNR PR00021132). Corrects the earlier '0 budget in P01' which only checked BPGE/overall — BPJA WRTTP=41 (GJAHR=2026) had the 10,000 USD entry. BPGE WRTTP=01 = overall-level; BPJA WRTTP=41 = annual current; BPJA WRTTP=42 = annual released; VERSN=000 throughout. Budget-exceeded message = BP/604 (PS-AVC engine, not FM-AVC). RESOLVED s-2026-07-01 (was open — see KU-2026-CJ32-RELEASE-NOT-LANDING, now closed): PS-AVC/BP-604 checks the RELEASED budget WRTTP=42 (set by CJ32), NOT the original/current WRTTP=41 (set by CJ30). Proof: WBS 650RER0008 (OBJNR PR00021132) has WRTTP=41=10,000 USD for FY2026 but WRTTP=42=0, and BP/604 still fires on a posting attempt — the WRTTP=41 entry alone does not satisfy AVC. Therefore CJ32 release is MANDATORY, not just CJ30; the two-step CJ30→CJ32 sequence is a hard AVC precondition, not merely bookkeeping.

claim: Cost-recovery WBS carry 0 PS-budget in BPGE on BOTH P01 and D01 (verified: 650RER0008 = 0 BPGE rows WHERE OBJNR LIKE PR*). Spendability of CR WBS comes from the FUND-level budget (633CRP9003, OBJNR FS*, claim #268/#287), NOT from a WBS-level PS-budget entry. Therefore a BP/604 (PS-AVC budget-exceeded) on a CR WBS in D01 signals a PS-AVC profile CONFIG DIFFERENCE (D01 has PS-AVC active; P01 relies on FM-AVC fund-level coverage for CR objects), not genuinely missing budget. claim: THREE LAYERS, NOT ONE (s097). Keying domains on SAP modules (FI, CO, MM, SD) conflates a TECHNICAL taxonomy with a business one: nobody in an organisation does 'FI', they pay an invoice or commit a budget, and every such act crosses several modules. Worse, `_module_to_domain` was ONE-TO-ONE and cannot be — FI-BL-PT pays suppliers (P2P), staff (payroll), travellers and treasury deals; PSM-FM serves B2C2A, P2P commitment checking, POST2BUDGET and PROJ2FUND. The model now separates COMPONENT (SAP's taxonomy, deterministic, not ours to rename) / DOMAIN (who owns it) / FLOW (what the organisation does end to end), with MANY-TO-MANY edges between all three. DECISION: do NOT rename domains to component codes — that would make a business layer look technical. Add the flow layer instead. PROCESS MINING RUNS ON FLOWS, never on modules, which is exactly why every vendor ships content named P2P/O2C/R2R. PUBLIC-SECTOR FLOWS WITH NO MARKET CONTENT: B2C2A (budget→commitment→actual, the primary financial control, FMRESERV 6.4M change docs), POST2BUDGET (position budgeting, 68 users), PROJ2FUND (PS 1.6M execs), GRANT2REPORT (no capability at all).

claim: ALGORITHMS ARE NESTED, not a flat list (s097, user insight). An algorithm's output is another's input: this is a directed graph with layers. L0 INVARIANT (component resolution, anchored on SAP itself) -> L0b CUSTOM OVERLAY (Z/Y objects, which SAP cannot resolve by definition) -> L1 OBSERVATION (logs, classification) -> L2 BOUNDARY (interface discovery, which PRODUCES the satellite catalogue) -> L3 ORIGIN (satellite derivation + the two-axis engine) -> L4 FLOW (process mining, per flow) -> L5 CONFORMANCE (needs a flow AND a normative model) -> L6 SELF-CHECK. THREE CONSEQUENCES: (1) an algorithm cannot be better than its dependencies — A3's origin resolution is capped by F1's parse quality; (2) improving a LOW layer lifts everything above it, measured: the L0 fix took the frontier from 40% to 7.7% without touching anything above; (3) the improvement mechanism must weight by DEPTH, which it does not yet.

claim: ALGORITHM ROADMAP from the state of the field, deduped against the closed research base (s097). Research w3t7ufrbg covers OCEL (34 refs), conformance (30), alignments (9), predictive (8) and NOTHING on declarative constraint mining, concept drift, LLM-assisted labelling or trace clustering. claim: ALGORITHM A8 — CHANGE-TO-EXECUTOR ATTRIBUTION, the generic enrichment. Built s097 by generalising the PBC analysis on the spot: joining a STATE-CHANGE stream to an EXECUTION stream on (user, day, hour) answers WHAT WRITES a thing for ANY domain, and the same shape answers which program sends an IDoc type, which job produces a file, which process touches an interface. THREE SCORINGS WERE WRONG BEFORE ONE WAS RIGHT, and this is the durable content. (1) RAW COINCIDENCE named a spool artifact `!QGYAO==========A_SEFI0410` as the writer of FMRESERV, because the RFC dispatcher runs constantly and coincides with everything. (2) LIFT removed that and INVERTED the error: it rewards rarity, so it ranked HUNCALC0 — the actual PBC engine — below noise and filtered it out at a 1.5 threshold. HUNCALC0 runs on 91 of 108 days, base rate 0.84, so its lift cannot exceed 1.19 however perfect the coincidence. AN ENGINE IS NOT RARE: running whenever the class changes is precisely what makes it the engine. (3) SMALL DENOMINATORS: a program that ran ONE day of 108 scored lift 27 on a single coincidence — the same defect as D6's z-score over a two-month baseline in different clothes. THE SCORE IS THE PHI COEFFICIENT over the 2x2 contingency table of (day,hour) slots: symmetric, correcting for both base rates, and a program present in every slot has d=0 so its margin collapses and it scores nothing. TWO CONSTRAINTS the user specified and that make it correct: TIME not day (2,493 hour slots vs 108 days — programs in the same nightly chain separate), and EXCLUSIVITY (a program claimed by >=5 classes is AMBIGUOUS; attributing one writer to every table is the failure the constraint prevents). CHANNEL CLASSIFICATION, from the user's second point: an EMPTY TCODE is not 'batch', it usually means a BAPI or RFC whose interface design never set one. So a dispatcher ranking high is EVIDENCE OF AN INTERFACE CHANNEL rather than noise to filter, and the calling function modules are named from PARAM3 — which is the hand-off into F1 (interface boundary) and F2 (satellites). Classes are labelled DIALOG / PROGRAM / INTERFACE. CONTROL RESULT: the algorithm independently recovers known-correct writers — RM_MEPO_GUI for EINKBELEG (purchase orders), RM_MEREQ_GUI for BANF (requisitions), the HR engine chain RHHCP_DC_EMPLOYEE / RHRFPM_ENGINE_PA30 for PBC and FMRESERV — while demoting SAPMSSY1 to AMBIGUOUS everywhere. 72 object classes, 3,280 programs, 2,493 slots.

claim: THERE IS NO VACANCY TOLERANCE — THE AUTHORED RULE P2B-3 DESCRIBES AN INTENT THE SYSTEM DOES NOT IMPLEMENT (s097, read from production source). P2B-3 states that 'a vacant post does not hold a commitment beyond its declared vacancy tolerance'. Read in P01: ZCL_IM__UNESCO_ENCUMB_VACANCY~DO_REQUIREMENT_FILTRATION delegates straight to DO_HANDLE_VACANCY, which only calls SUPER — so the vacancy filter is BINARY, vacant or not, with no duration term anywhere. Its DO_HANDLE_COMMITMENT_PERIOD is literally `ASSERT 1 = 2.` with the comment 'No filtering over period ==> in this scenario this is done in ZCL_IM__UNESCO_ENCUMB_ENCPER' — a deliberate guard saying this path must never execute. And ENCPER's IF_HRFPM_DC_PERIOD~OBJECT_GET_PERIOD does not bound the vacancy either: it takes the encumbrance validity interval and CUTS IT WITH THE OBJECT'S OWN EXISTENCE INTERVAL. SO A VACANT POST HOLDS ITS COMMITMENT FOR THE WHOLE FUNDING WINDOW, however long it has been vacant. Three things bound the commitment and NONE of them is a tolerance: the encumbrance interval/biennium (PBC-R3), the object's existence interval (this method), and the extension horizon MV_EXTENSION_YEARS (PBC-R4). claim: THE ATTRIBUTION FINDING IS ALSO A LICENSING FINDING, AND IT IS THE FIRST CONCRETE CONTENT FOR R_S4_READINESS (s097, user insight). The same measurement that shows 5.3M calls with no attributable actor also describes the tenant's DIGITAL ACCESS exposure, because SAP licenses indirect use by DOCUMENTS CREATED THROUGH NON-DIALOG CHANNELS — which is precisely what algorithm A8 already derives per object class. THE STRUCTURE OF THE RISK. Today, a satellite calling over RFC under a technical account costs a system-user licence and nothing per call. On S/4HANA — and far more sharply on S/4HANA CLOUD — that same traffic is API consumption and Digital Access documents. This tenant's operating model is 80% external, so the exposure is not a detail of the migration: it is the shape of the migration. Every integration that is free today becomes a metered cost. WHAT MAKES IT MEASURABLE RIGHT NOW, with no new extraction: A8 classifies each object class by write channel, and the classes written through RFC_INBOUND are exactly the candidates for Digital Access counting. FMRESERV alone carries 6,951,908 change documents; the named writers already include BAPI_PO_CREATE1, BAPI_PR_CREATE, BAPI_INCOMINGINVOICE_CREATE1, BAPI_GOODSMVT_CREATE and ZBAPI_VENDOR_CREATE2 — all document-creating calls from outside. AND THE OPAQUE ACCOUNTS ARE THE WORST CASE TWICE OVER. MULESOFT (3.23M calls, one identity), BRIDGE-RFC (2.11M, no caller field) and UBO-RFC (324K) cannot be attributed to a person — so they can be neither excused as named-user activity nor apportioned to a business owner. In a licensing negotiation, traffic you cannot attribute is traffic you cannot defend. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR THE MODEL: R_S4_READINESS was the ONE completely empty column across all 21 domains. It now has its first anchor, and the anchor is commercial rather than technical — which is probably why it stayed empty: we were looking for technical readiness factors.

So a NOT_IMPLEMENTED verdict against a superseded blueprint says the design became irrelevant, not that the system failed. claim: THE SEVEN-DIMENSIONAL BCS RUNS AS THREE DIMENSIONS (s097, measured against the SAP-standard coding block from the UN Secretariat's Umoja reference). Across 2,308,814 FM line items in fmifiit_full: Fund (FONDS) 100%, Funds Center (FISTL) 100%, Commitment Item (FIPEX) 100% — and then four empty. Funded Program (MEASURE) 0.0%. Functional Area (FAREA) 0.0%, its only distinct value being blank. Grant 0%, consistent with GM having zero tables. Budget Period column absent entirely. THIS IS NOT A SHORTFALL AT THE MARGIN: four of seven dimensions carry no value in a single row out of 2.3 million. FUNCTIONAL AREA IS THE ONE THAT SHOULD ALARM. BBP-04 defines it as UNESCO's C/5 EXPECTED RESULTS — the programme structure, used for STATUTORY REPORTING BY PROGRAMME OBJECTIVE. It is the dimension that ties money to purpose, and it is blank in every row, which means budget consumption cannot be reported by programme objective from FM at all. For an organisation whose mandate is literally expressed as C/5 Expected Results, that is the gap worth taking to the business. FUNDED PROGRAM BEING EMPTY EXPLAINS SOMETHING BOTH PROJECTS HAD ONLY OBSERVED. It is the designed WBS-to-FM bridge. Our model and theirs both carry PROJ.PSPID = GEBER — project-as-fund — and both label it a STATIC PROXY without explaining why it survives. It survives because the designed bridge dimension carries nothing: the fund code is the only project link that exists. Two open questions turn out to be one answered fact. METHOD NOTE: this is the first measurement in the project made against a genuinely SAP-STANDARD yardstick rather than against UNESCO's own design intent. BBP-04 says what UNESCO intended; the Umoja coding block says what SAP expects a public-sector posting to carry. Measuring against the second is a different and stronger claim, and it is why the peer material was ranked first among the S_STANDARD_REF sources.

claim: THE BUDGET RATE MECHANISM WAS DESIGNED AWAY AND BUILT ANYWAY — and its failure mode is the reason it was designed away (s097, BBP-08 against production). BBP-08 calls it 'the most significant simplification': the practice of a special CONSTANT EXCHANGE RATE for EUR-to-USD conversion IN BUDGET EXECUTION is ELIMINATED. Constant dollar becomes strictly a REPORTING concept, an extra BW column. Budget control instead uses an additional AVC in BCS with a tolerance (~105%) RATHER THAN MANIPULATING POSTING EXCHANGE RATES — expressly so that postings use operational rates, for IPSAS. WHAT EXISTS IN PRODUCTION IS THE OPPOSITE: YCL_FM_BR_EXCHANGE_RATE_BL manipulates the exchange rate during budget execution. And it carries a one-line defect confirmed in source — the conversion gate appends only 'EUR' to mr_waers, so a USD posting exits via CHECK without setting rv_is_ok and the conversion is SKIPPED SILENTLY. A trace recorded 42 invocations of the class and ZERO reads of TCURR: it fired and converted nothing. MEASURED BLAST RADIUS, already established in INC-BUDGETRATE-EQG and now attached to the rule: 458 funds carry EUR-loaded reservations with USD consumption; 135,792 bypass postings lifetime; $375,011,484.95 of volume; ~$35.7M of theoretical AVC drift exposure; 70 funds still exposed in 2026 with 214 bypass postings already made. WHY THIS IS THE CLEAREST DEMONSTRATION IN THE PROJECT OF WHY S_STANDARD_REF MATTERS: without the as-designed reference the incident reads as 'a bug to fix'. With it, the same facts read as 'a mechanism the blueprint explicitly eliminated was implemented, and the failure it produces is the very reason for the elimination'. The design's alternative — an AVC tolerance in BCS — cannot have this failure class at all, because it never touches the posting rate. Same evidence, different conclusion, and a different remedy: fix the gate, or retire the mechanism for what BBP-08 specified. AND AN IPSAS ANGLE THAT IS NOT OURS TO DECIDE: the design's stated reason for the deletion was that postings must use OPERATIONAL exchange rates. A mechanism that overrides the posting rate is therefore not merely fragile — it sits against the standard the design was aligning to. That is a question for the business.

THE APPLICABILITY PERIMETER IS EIGHT DIMENSIONS, all of which must pass, each a CHECK that exits silently: ledger = 9A (note: NOT the AVC ledger 9H); company code = UNES; FM area = UNES; business area = GEF; currency = EUR ONLY (the defect); commitment item EXCLUDES GAINS and REVENUE; transaction EXCLUDES HRM1/HRM2/HRP1, so PBC pre-commitment, PBC commitment and payroll are OUT of the main path; and fund type IN a DATA-DRIVEN set from FMFUNDTYPE WHERE ZZFIX_RATE = X — measured in P01 as 14 types, all UNES (001-005, 009, 010, 012, 013, 016-018, 094, 095), i.e. Regular Programme only. Earmarked 101-115, MBF 299 and CRP 311/314 are NOT in the perimeter. THERE IS AN ACTIVATION SWITCH NOBODY HAD RECORDED: CHECK_BR_IS_ACTIVE compares sy-datum against MV_START_DATE, read from the TVARVC variable Y_FM_FIXED_RATE_START. Measured in P01: 20240101, so BR has been active since 1 January 2024. THE TRAP: if that variable is missing, the code defaults the date to '99991231' and BR silently never activates — a kill switch that fails closed and says nothing. THREE GATES, NOT ONE, and the difference between them is where the asymmetry lives. CHECK_CONDITIONS is the main path: EUR only, PBC and payroll excluded. CHECK_CONDITIONS_2 is the STAFF path: it accepts EUR *and* USD and INCLUDES HRM1/HRM2/HRP1 — so the cure for the currency defect exists inside the class and is unreachable from the main path. CHECK_CONDITIONS_3 is the complement, used for DELETION during RFFMREPO reconstruction: inverted membership on ledger/company/FM-area/business-area, and it INCLUDES what the others exclude. A SECOND LATENT DEFECT, NEW: the staff gate also checks IV_HKONT IN MR_HKONT, and MR_HKONT is DECLARED at line 57 and NEVER POPULATED anywhere in the class. In ABAP a value IN an empty range is FALSE, so whenever a GL account is passed the staff gate FAILS ALWAYS. Same shape as the known mr_waers defect — a range that gates and is never filled — and it means the one path that would have handled USD is itself closed on that condition.

BBP-06 states the AS-IS it set out to replace: donor agreements tracked OUTSIDE SAP in SPREADSHEETS and SISTER, 'with only indirect representation through MISUSED FUND AND WBS MASTER DATA OBJECTS'. claim: THE B2R YARDSTICK IS THE AS-RUN, NOT THE BLUEPRINT — frame correction on my own ingest (s097, user-directed). WHAT I DID WRONG: I read the 2017 BBPs and measured production against them, producing 17 rules whose verdicts were mostly NOT_IMPLEMENTED. The MEASUREMENTS are real and stand — nine FM areas, zero gm* tables, 18 commitment items, Functional Area and Funded Program blank across 2,308,814 rows. THE FRAME WAS WRONG. Measuring against a superseded design turns 'the organisation built something else' into 'the system failed', and those are different claims with different remedies. WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED, measured from both ends independently: UNESCO kept SAP as the SYSTEM OF RECORD and moved the SYSTEM OF ENGAGEMENT entirely outside it — Salesforce / Core Planner, ORION, named-user portals. Not around SAP; IN FRONT OF it. The peer project derived this from the Salesforce event log (23,730 status events, 26,075 posting events); we derived the same model from the SAP audit log (15.6M RFC calls). Two instruments, one model. THE REAL B2R END-TO-END, measured per workplan on real timestamps: plan to Validated median 20.9 DAYS (p90 428) — the human planning loop; Validated to first SAP posting median 1.8 DAYS — the integration seam; 5,929 workplans reached SAP and 91.7% carry a Financial_Summary return; 26,075 posting events of which 82.9% are budget transfers. SO THE BOTTLENECK IS HUMAN VALIDATION, NOT TECHNOLOGY AND NOT CONFIGURATION. The cross-system handoff is near-instant. Any B2R improvement effort aimed at SAP configuration is aimed at the fast part. THE FAILURE MODES ARE NAMED AND ATTRIBUTED: the forward sync is SERIAL and STOP-ON-FIRST-ERROR, so one failing object halts an entire workplan. 103 workplans and 354 allocations carry errors — fund create/assign ~130 (top single error: 'Assignment to 43 C/5 not possible with fund validity 01.01.2024-31.12.2025', 39 times), project create ~67. And INT-05, the Fund Center master channel SAP to Core Planner, has been BLOCKED SINCE 2023. THE WARNING WAS ALREADY WRITTEN IN THEIR OWN WORK. knowledge/36 re-scored one of its own claims with this exact diagnosis — the 'manual entry' reading of FC/CC/FA was 'a DESIGN-DOC ARTIFACT OVERTAKEN BY THE AS-RUN' — and deprecates any dialog-based baseline outright: 'a redesign baselined on dialog usage is baselined on <20% of the real traffic'. I walked into the failure mode their document names. WHAT THE BBP INGEST IS STILL WORTH: archaeology and vocabulary. The AVC address triple named a distinction we had measured and could not name, and that keeps its value. The rest is a record of what was intended, not a scorecard for what is.

claim: THE MODEL DIMENSIONS LIVE IN THE IDENTIFIER STRING, NOT IN THE SCHEMA — measured end-to-end on the golden (s098, ALGORITHM A10). THE FM LEDGER POSTS ON EXACTLY TWO LEGS. In fmifiit_full, 2,308,814 actual lines: FONDS 100%, FISTL 100%, FIPEX 100% — and MEASURE (Funded Program), FAREA (Functional Area), GRANT_NBR and PRCTR are populated in 0.0%. MEASURE is the DESIGNED WBS-to-FM bridge, so the designed chain from work to money does not exist in the data. AND THERE IS NO FOREIGN KEY EITHER. prps carries no fund and no fund-centre column; proj carries none. Nothing in the PS master points at FM. YET THE CHAIN RESOLVES AT 99.5%, THROUGH THE STRING. Every WBS identifier is <fund code>.<level>.<level>: taking the root before the first dot, 59,424 of 59,749 WBS elements land on a real fund. The project id IS a fund code — 13,812 of 13,976 PSPID values (98.8%), the project-as-fund inversion the 2017 design explicitly forbade, still load-bearing. The 4-level spine is dot DEPTH, not a parent key. THE GRAMMAR IS ALSO A CLASSIFICATION. Three code families coexist in funds.FINCODE and each predicts the TYPE family: all-numeric 8 or 10 digits (73.2% of the UNES master) for RP/staff types 0xx; NNN+GEO+NNNN (20.8%) for extrabudgetary delivery types 1xx; alpha-prefixed legacy variants for older VC types. Fund centres are 3-letter organisational acronyms (84.0%). SO THE IMPLICIT TAXONOMY IS REAL AND IT IS THE OPERATING MODEL: the filters, groupings and hierarchies the business uses daily are encoded in identifier positions that no foreign key, no data dictionary and no migration tool can see. WHY THIS IS THE FINDING AND NOT A CURIOSITY: a link that works through a string convention is invisible to anyone reading the data model. It is never documented, never load-tested, and — the part that costs money — never migrated. An S/4 conversion that rebuilds the schema faithfully, not knowing the semantics live in the strings, carries none of this across.

claim: FUND RESERVATIONS ARE LONG-LIVED AND REPEATEDLY ADJUSTED, ON A BIENNIUM RHYTHM — NOT A MONTHLY ONE (s098, measured on 6,415,467 FMRESERV change headers). THE OPERATOR'S RECOLLECTION was that reservations are adjusted MONTH BY MONTH so the funds are never released. The data confirms the RETENTION and refutes the MONTHLY. WHAT IS MEASURED: 874,143 distinct reservation documents carry 6,415,467 changes, 7.3 per document on average — and FMRESERV is the largest change-document class in the system. Among documents that live SIX MONTHS OR MORE (416,680 of them), the median document is touched in 32% of the months it exists, with a median of 6 changes, and only 12% are touched in 80% or more of their months. So they are maintained repeatedly across a long life, not topped up every month. THE LIFETIME DISTRIBUTION IS THE REAL SIGNAL, and it is not smooth. It spikes hard at structural boundaries: 145,354 documents live exactly 13 months and 87,353 live exactly 25 months. Twenty-five months is a BIENNIUM. These reservations are created and carried to the end of a budget period rather than consumed and closed — which is the retention behaviour the recollection describes, running on the budget calendar instead of the monthly one. The 25-month cohort also carries the highest adjustment count, a median of 11 changes each. THE ARTIFACT THAT NEARLY PRODUCED A WRONG ANSWER, recorded because it is the more useful lesson: measured over ALL documents the ratio of months-with-a-change to months-of-life has a MEDIAN OF 0.96, which reads as 'touched in essentially every month of its life' and would have confirmed the monthly reading outright. It is an artifact. A document created and closed inside one month scores 1.00 by construction, and 34.7% of documents live exactly one month. Excluding short lives moves the median from 0.96 to 0.32. THE RATIO WAS MEASURING DOCUMENT LIFETIME, NOT ADJUSTMENT BEHAVIOUR. WHAT REMAINS OPEN: whether the AMOUNT moves down in step with consumption (a genuine commitment drawdown) or is restored (a hold). That needs the value history in CDPOS, which is deliberately deferred, or the amounts in fmioi joined per document.

evidence_for.cite: 874,143 documents / 6,415,467 changes / 7.3 avg; life>=6 months n=416,680 median ratio 0.32, median 6 changes, 12.0% at >=0.8; lifetime spikes at 13 months n=145,354 and 25 months n=87,353; all-documents median ratio 0.96 is an artifact of 34.7% single-month lives

resolution_notes: First of the operator's B2R recollections put to data. The retention behaviour is real; the monthly cadence is not. Recorded with the artifact intact because the artifact is the transferable lesson: a ratio whose denominator is a lifetime measures the lifetime unless the short lives are excluded.

claim: FUNDED PROGRAM IS EMPTY BECAUSE THE DERIVATION THAT WOULD FILL IT WAS NEVER CONFIGURED — the causal chain, closed with evidence from P01 (s098). THE QUESTION THIS ANSWERS: MEASURE (Funded Program) is populated in 0.0% of 2,308,814 FM actual lines. That could mean the designed chain was switched OFF, or that it was never BUILT. Those are different findings with different remedies, and until now we could not tell them apart. FOUR MEASUREMENTS, IN ORDER. (1) SAP's own rule: Funded Program is never assigned directly — in integrated postings its account assignment is ALWAYS DERIVED at posting time, via FMDERIVE, and it is BCS-only. (2) The derivation tool holds NO STRATEGY: T811C, T811S and T811K are EMPTY in P01, verified with and without a TAB='FMDERIVE' filter, returning zero rows rather than an error. (3) FMDERIVE IS NOT EVEN A REGISTERED DERIVATION POINT: T811X registers exactly four — CCSS, CEST7, GLPCT, JBDST7 — and FMDERIVE is not among them. (4) MEANWHILE THE MECHANISM ACTUALLY IN USE IS THE CLASSIC ONE AND IT IS FULLY POPULATED: TABADRSF carries 3,627 derivation rule rows, with TABADRST 253, TABADRS 170, TABADRX 43, TABADRH 32 and TABADRPCONF 20. THE CONCLUSION IS STRUCTURAL, NOT ACCIDENTAL. UNESCO derives FM account assignments through the CLASSIC account-assignment derivation, which fills Fund, Fund Center and Commitment Item — exactly the three that measure 100% — and which CANNOT derive Funded Program. The mechanism that can derive it, the derivation tool behind FMDERIVE, was never configured at all. So the empty column is not neglect and not a switch that someone turned off: the organisation runs a derivation architecture in which that dimension has no way to be filled. WHY IT MATTERS FOR WHAT COMES NEXT: every proposal to 'start using Funded Program' is really a proposal to stand up a second derivation mechanism and migrate onto it, which is a different size of change from configuring a field. And it explains why the identifier convention exists — the grammar is not a shortcut around a working feature, it is the only carrier available under the architecture actually in place.

claim: THE FUND-CENTRE HIERARCHY IS VERSIONED BY THE PROGRAMMATIC DOCUMENT, AND ONE FM POSTING IN FIVE ROLLS UP NOWHERE (s098, ALGORITHM A12, traversed from the sets extracted this session). SO THE ORGANISATIONAL AXIS HANGS FROM THE PROGRAMMATIC ONE, and it is re-issued each biennium. That is why 272 fund centres appear in several root trees — versioning, not a defect: a report must CHOOSE a biennium, and one that does not will mix two. Measured separately, repetition INSIDE a single tree is ZERO, so a roll-up within one biennium does not double count. THE FINDING THAT MATTERS: COVERAGE. claim: SET CLASSES MUST BE IDENTIFIED BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY CONVENTION — a method rule paid for twice in one session (s098). I named SET CLASS 0102 as the fund centres from the standard SAP convention; it is GL account groups, matching the fund-centre master at 0.0%. Correcting that, I then declared CLASS 0303 as 'numeric fund centres' on a 79.3% leaf match; traversed, only 9 of its 505 reached values are real fund centres and its nodes are named CS01-4000 and COI-6-0200 — a cost-centre structure. THE RULE: identify a set class by traversing it and testing the reached values against the master, and treat a high match on short numeric codes as no evidence at all. claim: THE SYSTEM ROLLS UP BY WHAT IS SPENT, NOT BY WHO SPENDS IT (s098, AN-ORG-ROLLUP-IS-IT-ALIVE). The question was what actually produces organisational totals, since the fund-centre set hierarchy is frozen and unread. The answer is that no organisation dimension is rolled up at all. FM'S OWN HIERARCHY TABLES SETTLE IT. FMHICTR — the FUND CENTRE hierarchy — returns ZERO rows. FMHICI — the COMMITMENT ITEM hierarchy — and FMHIVARNT, the hierarchy variants, both carry data. So in FM's native structures the cost-category hierarchy is built and the organisational one is not. AND THE REPORTING LAYER IS VERY MUCH ALIVE, which corrects the impression left by looking only at custom code. In the four-month audit window the standard FM reports run at scale: RFFMEPGAX 17,505 executions across 441 USERS, RFFMRE01 13,433 / 323 users, transaction FMX3 11,415 / 346 users, FMRP_RFFMEP1FX 7,451 / 195 users. There is even RFFMAVC_HIER_VIEW, 426 executions / 72 users — a hierarchy view, running on the hierarchy that exists. SO THE THREE FACTS FIT TOGETHER. The custom programmes that read sets read class 0102, GL ACCOUNT groups. FM's built hierarchy is the commitment-item one. AVC collapses commitment items into grouped buckets. Every structure that is maintained is a structure of WHAT the money is spent on. The organisational axis — who spends it — has a master, has a set class, and has no built hierarchy, no maintenance and no reader. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ORPHAN FINDING: the 20.6% of FM lines posting to fund centres outside the set hierarchy do not distort any total in use, because no total in use is organisational. It is not a reporting defect. It is a dimension the organisation does not report on, and the earlier framing of it as a silent under-report was wrong.

claim: THE BUDGET RATE SOLUTION MAINTAINS A PARALLEL FM LEDGER, AND NONE OF IT IS EXTRACTED — the largest single knowledge gap now open (s098, found from the user's lead: look at what uses FMIOI). IT DOES NOT CONVERT IN PLACE. YCL_FI_BR_UPDATE_TABLES has exactly three methods — UPDATE_BR_FMIFIIT, UPDATE_BR_FMIOI, UPDATE_BR_FM_POS — and each one reads a CUSTOM table keyed identically to its standard counterpart, then UPDATEs it if the line is already there and INSERTs it if not. The fixed-rate amounts live in ZFKBTR and ZTRBTR, alongside a full audit stamp: CPUDT, CPUTM, USNAM, TCODE per line. SO THERE IS A SHADOW LEDGER: YTFM_BR_FMIFIIT shadows the FM ACTUAL line items, YTFM_BR_FMIOI shadows the COMMITMENTS — the fund reservations — and YTFM_BR_FM_POS holds encumbrance positions with ENC_TYPE and BETRG_BEFORE, an explicit before-and-after trail. THE PERSONNEL PATH HAS ITS OWN TABLES, which confirms the operator's recollection that BR for staff runs through payroll: YTFM_BR_PAYPI (referenced 15 times in the corpus), YTFM_BR_PAYPH (9) and YTFM_BR_PAYPER (5). Plus YTFM_BR_REP_H and YTFM_BR_REP_D for the reporting layer. ALL EIGHT EXIST IN P01 AND CARRY DATA — probed, all narrow enough to read in one pass — AND NOT ONE IS IN THE GOLDEN. Every claim we hold about the budget rate is derived from SOURCE CODE and never from the amounts the mechanism actually produced. We can say what it is designed to do and we cannot say what it did. THIS ALSO REFRAMES THE EARLIER DEFECT FINDINGS. The EUR-only perimeter and the never-populated MR_HKONT range are code facts; whether they cost anything is a question about the shadow ledger, and the shadow ledger is exactly what is missing.

claim: THE BUDGET RATE CHANGES THE VALUE AT POSTING TIME, IN THE STANDARD TABLES — there is no parallel ledger (s098, user correction, confirmed by extraction). THE MECHANISM: the enhancements modify the STANDARD POSTING, converting the amount at the moment it is written. So the fixed-rate value lands in FMIFIIT and FMIOI themselves, and there is nothing to reconcile a shadow against. This is why the PERIMETER and the THREE GATES are not context but the entire mechanism: they decide, per posting, whether conversion happens before the write. THE EVIDENCE THAT SETTLES IT. The YTFM_BR_* tables that would constitute a shadow ledger are EMPTY: YTFM_BR_FMIOI 0 rows and YTFM_BR_FM_POS 0 rows — the latter is the BETRG_BEFORE before-and-after trail, never populated. YTFM_BR_REP_H holds 38,894 rows and is a REPORTING structure, the only one of the family in real use. YTFM_BR_FMIFIIT remains unmeasured; P01 dropped before it. THE PERSONNEL PATH IS BARELY ALIVE: 1,048 payroll items against 12 headers and 703 period rows. This is the first hard evidence bearing on AN-BR-HKONT-EMPTY-RANGE — the staff gate tests IV_HKONT against a range declared at line 57 and never populated, an empty range makes IN false in ABAP, and the payroll tables are near-empty. The two agree; neither proves the other alone. WHAT IT CHANGES FOR MEASUREMENT: the effect of the budget rate cannot be measured by diffing a shadow against the standard, because there is no shadow. It has to be measured inside the standard tables — for lines inside the perimeter, what rate was applied against what the standard rate would have given. Harder, and the right question. AND THE METHOD LESSON, which is the same one this session keeps paying for: I read UPDATE and INSERT methods in a class and concluded a ledger existed, without asking whether the target tables held a single row. A writer with empty targets is a path that was built and is not used, and that is a different finding entirely.

claim: THE BUDGET RATE, MEASURED — the perimeter is about 10,400 lines a year and 2024 is not recorded at all (s098, YTFM_BR_FMIFIIT extracted). WHAT THE TABLE IS. Not a parallel ledger — that reading was wrong and is superseded. YTFM_BR_FMIFIIT is a RECORD OF BR-AFFECTED POSTINGS: 12,852 rows, and every single one matches the perimeter read from the class. 100% FIKRS=UNES, 100% TWAER=EUR, 100% RLDNR=9A. The perimeter derived from source and the perimeter present in the data agree exactly, which is two instruments reaching the same answer. AND IT IS ESSENTIALLY COMPLETE. Applying the real perimeter to the standard ledger — UNES, EUR, a fund whose type carries ZZFIX_RATE (14 types, 40,871 funds), commitment item excluding GAINS and REVENUE, transaction excluding HRM1/HRM2/HRP1 — gives 10,400 lines in 2025 against 10,383 recorded: 99.8%. In 2026 the count runs slightly OVER the filter (2,469 against 2,013), which means the real perimeter is marginally wider than the eight dimensions reconstructed from source, not narrower. THE PERIMETER IS SMALL IN ABSOLUTE TERMS. About 10,400 lines a year against 985,255 FM actual lines in 2025 — roughly 1.1% of the ledger passes through the mechanism. AND 2024 IS EMPTY. The activation variable Y_FM_FIXED_RATE_START holds 20240101 and the perimeter for 2024 contains 10,660 lines, yet the table holds ZERO rows for that year and its earliest processing stamp is 2025-01-13. Two readings fit and the data does not choose between them: either the recording table was introduced a year after the mechanism, or the mechanism did not run in its first declared year. The distinction matters for anyone reconciling 2024 and it is not settled here. THE CURRENCY GATE, IN PROPORTION. The main gate accepts EUR only. EUR is 478,888 of 2,308,814 FM lines — 20.7%. USD is 1,216,134 — 52.7%. So the mechanism is scoped to a currency that is a fifth of the ledger while the majority currency runs outside the main path, and the one gate that accepts USD is CHECK_CONDITIONS_2, the staff gate, whose HKONT range is declared and never populated. WHO WRITES IT: named users through dialog FI transactions — FB01 5,019, blank 4,671, FB60 949, MIRO 929, FB50 663. So the affected population is dialog-driven document entry, not an interface or a batch.

claim: THE FIXED BUDGET RATE IS 1.0416667 — recovered from data, and it is NOT what the FM actual lines carry (s098, the control table reviewed at the user's request). WHAT THE CONTROL TABLE GAVE UP. YTFM_BR_FMIFIIT was a CONTROL table that was ultimately not used, and reviewing it anyway paid: joined to the standard FM lines on its full key, 12,396 of its 12,852 rows match a real line, and the comparison is unambiguous. ZTRBTR EQUALS TRBTR in 100% of them — the transaction amount is untouched. ZFKBTR DIFFERS from FKBTR in 99.7%. And the ratio ZFKBTR/ZTRBTR is CONSTANT at 1.0416667, which is exactly 1/0.96, while FKBTR/TRBTR varies around 1.095 — the market. So the control table holds the FIXED-rate valuation and the standard line holds the MARKET-rate valuation, and the fixed rate itself is now known as a number rather than as a concept. WHERE IT IS NOT. Searching the standard FM actual lines for that exact ratio, inside the perimeter — UNES, EUR, a fund of one of the 14 ZZFIX_RATE types, excluding GAINS/REVENUE and HRM1/HRM2/HRP1 — finds it on 19 of 9,737 lines in 2024 (0.2%), 9 of 9,713 in 2025 (0.1%) and 0 of 1,800 in 2026. The control group makes that decisive: OUTSIDE the perimeter, in the same year and currency, the ratio appears on 2,735 of 105,501 lines — 2.59%. The rate shows up LESS OFTEN INSIDE THE PERIMETER THAN OUTSIDE IT, so those few matches are coincidence and not mechanism. NOR IS IT IN THE BUDGET. Every EUR line in bpja carries an implied rate of exactly 1.0 and no perimeter fund appears among them at all. SO WHAT THE MECHANISM CHANGES IS NOT THE FKBTR-TO-TRBTR RELATIONSHIP IN FMIFIIT, AND NOT THE EUR BUDGET. Two candidate locations are eliminated by measurement. The user states the enhancements modify the standard posting at write time, and the enhancement sources are the one part of the family we cannot read — EXT-ENHO-SOURCE is blocked — so the field they touch is not yet identified. That is an honest open state and a much better one than the two confident wrong answers that preceded it in this session.

claim: THE BUDGET RATE IS EXCHANGE RATE TYPE EURX, IT LIVES IN THE FM LEDGER ONLY, AND THE FM-TO-FI DIFFERENCE IS THE REPORTED IMPACT (s098 — the user named the rate type and the design; both are confirmed by measurement). THE DESIGN, as stated by the user and consistent with everything measured: the solution modifies the FUNDS MANAGEMENT ledger ONLY and leaves FI/GL on the standard rate. That way the budget is stated at a fixed rate while the general ledger stays correct, which is what makes it acceptable to audit. The difference between FM and FI/GL is then REPORTED, and that difference IS the budget-rate impact. THE RATE TYPE. Not M. EURX — a dedicated table of 60 entries over 55 currency pairs, against 54,790 entries for M. For USD/EUR it holds 1.09529, valid from 2024-01-01 and re-entered unchanged on 2024-12-01. A rate type with 60 rows is not a market feed; it is a fixed table. AND IT IS MEASURABLY IN THE FM LINES. Inside the perimeter — UNES, EUR, a fund of one of the 14 ZZFIX_RATE types, excluding GAINS/REVENUE and HRM1/HRM2/HRP1 — the ratio FKBTR/TRBTR equals the EURX rate on 9,196 of 9,713 lines in 2025 (94.7%) and 1,748 of 1,800 in 2026 (97.1%). OUTSIDE the perimeter, same year and currency, it appears on 25 of 29,307 lines — 0.09%. A separation of roughly a thousandfold. That is the mechanism, visible in the data. AND 2024 WAS PARTIAL: 740 of 9,737 perimeter lines, 7.6%. So the mechanism did run in its first declared year and ran on a small share of it, reaching full coverage in 2025. That answers the 2024 question from the postings themselves rather than from the control table, whose emptiness in 2024 turned out to say nothing about the mechanism. THIS CORRECTS MY OWN PREVIOUS CLAIM. I reported that the fixed rate is NOT present in the FM actual lines, with a control group appearing to prove it. The measurement was sound and the NUMBER WAS WRONG: I searched for 1.0416667, taken from the unused control table, and labelled the 1.09529 lines 'the market' without ever checking what rate type produced them. The real fixed rate was sitting in the data I had already looked at, on the lines I had already counted, under a name I had not asked for. THE METHOD LESSON, and it is the sharpest of this session: a control group makes a negative result look rigorous, and it cannot save a test that is looking for the wrong value. Before concluding that something is absent, establish what it would look like FROM THE CONFIGURATION — here, one query to TCURR for the rate types in use — rather than from a derived artefact.

evidence_for.cite: EURX: 60 entries over 55 currency pairs vs M 54,790; USD/EUR 1.09529 from 2024-01-01, re-entered 2024-12-01; perimeter lines at EURX 740/9,737 (7.6%) 2024, 9,196/9,713 (94.7%) 2025, 1,748/1,800 (97.1%) 2026; outside perimeter 25/29,307 (0.09%)

Both statements confirmed. AN-BR-WHERE-DOES-THE-VALUE-LAND closed.

On route 1 it did not run: the UN operational rate itself equalled 1.09529 from 15 January and again from 15 August 2024, so FI posted at that rate and FM inherited it. claim: THE BUDGET-RATE PERIMETER IS EIGHT CONDITIONS AND EACH ONE IS SKIPPED WHEN THE CALLER PASSES IT EMPTY — so it is not a filter (s098, user direction: the conditions are in the classes, it is fund type AND currency AND more, and it is very specific). THE EIGHT, from the CONSTRUCTOR and CHECK_CONDITIONS: ledger 9A · company code UNES · FM area UNES · BUSINESS AREA GEF · currency EUR · commitment item EXCLUDING GAINS and REVENUE · business transaction EXCLUDING HRM1, HRM2 and HRP1 — PBC pre-commitment, PBC commitment and payroll posting · fund type among those flagged ZZFIX_RATE in FMFUNDTYPE for FM area UNES, measured as exactly 14. AND THE SEMANTICS THAT MATTER MORE THAN THE LIST. Every condition in CHECK_CONDITIONS is wrapped in IF IV_xxx IS NOT INITIAL. A parameter the caller leaves EMPTY SKIPS ITS CONDITION ENTIRELY. So the effective perimeter is whichever subset of the eight the caller actually supplies, two callers can get different perimeters from the same class, and nothing records which. The perimeter cannot be reproduced as a WHERE clause over the FM lines, and any measurement built that way is an approximation by construction. ONE CONDITION IS UNMEASURABLE FROM THE DATA SIDE: business area GEF is not carried on the FM line at all. So the perimeter I measured — UNES, EUR, the 14 fund types, minus GAINS/REVENUE, minus the three HR transactions — is a SUPERSET of the real one. That means the 94.7% of 2025 lines found at the EURX rate is an UNDERSTATEMENT: the true coverage against the true perimeter is higher. THE OTHER TWO GATES INVERT IT. Gate 2, the staff path, accepts EUR and USD and INCLUDES the three HR transactions that gate 1 excludes — and additionally checks IV_HKONT against a range declared at line 57 and never populated, which makes it FALSE whenever a GL account is passed. Gate 3, used for deletion during RFFMREPO reconstruction, is the complement throughout: the fund-type SELECT is repeated with sign 'E', and GAINS, REVENUE and the HR transactions are INCLUDED rather than excluded.

evidence_for.cite: CONSTRUCTOR appends 9A / UNES / UNES / GEF / EUR, MR_FIPEX sign E on GAINS and REVENUE, MR_VRGNG sign E on HRM1/HRM2/HRP1, MR_FUND_TYPE from FMFUNDTYPE ZZFIX_RATE; CHECK_CONDITIONS wraps each CHECK in IF IV_xxx IS NOT INITIAL

claim: THE BUDGET-RATE IMPACT MEASURED: MINUS 1.22 MILLION USD OVER 9,407 VERIFIED LINE PAIRS IN 2025-2026 (s098, AN-BR-IMPACT-AMOUNT). THE DESIGN IS CONFIRMED LINE BY LINE. For the same document line, on the same EUR base amount, FM carries the FIXED EURX rate and FI/GL carries a VARYING rate: base 1,408.80 EUR gives FM 1,543.04 USD at 1.09529 and FI 1,437.55 USD at 1.02041; base 1,800.00 gives FM 1,971.52 at 1.09529 and FI 1,875.00 at 1.04167. The FI rates observed run across 1.02041, 1.04167, 1.11483, 1.14679, 1.15607, 1.16822, 1.17096, 1.17233 — a moving standard rate — while FM stays on 1.09529 throughout. Exactly the stated design: the budget is fixed, the general ledger is correct, and the difference is the impact. THE NUMBER. Over 9,407 pairs verified one-to-one with a matching base amount: FM totals 63,159,380.79 USD, FI/GL totals 64,383,111.62 USD, and the difference is -1,223,730.83 USD — about -1.9% of the FI base. NEGATIVE, meaning the budget absorbed LESS than the general ledger recorded, because the fixed rate sits below most of the standard rates in force across the period. THE BOUNDS, stated because they are real. This covers the 1:1 pairs whose base amounts agree — 9,407 of roughly 11,000 perimeter lines at EURX in those years, about 86%. The perimeter itself is a SUPERSET, because business area GEF is not carried on the FM line and cannot be filtered from the data side. And 2024 is EXCLUDED from this figure: its 740 EURX lines pair to FI lines carrying the SAME 1.09529 rate, so FM and FI agree and the difference is zero — a different situation that needs its own explanation rather than being averaged in. WHAT IT TOOK. Two wrong joins on the way, both caught by inspecting pairs instead of trusting a total: the first omitted the company code from the key, so document numbers collided across company codes and matched 4,000 USD against 1,875; the second compared signed FM amounts to unsigned BSEG amounts and produced a 152-million-dollar 'impact' that was pure sign error. Neither survived looking at six rows side by side.

claim: THE ORGANISATION'S OWN CONTROL DEFINES THE BUDGET-RATE IMPACT, AND IT SUBTRACTS IT TO FIND THE REAL RECONCILIATION BREAK (s098, YFM_FI_COMPARE_INCLUDING_BR extracted from P01 at the user's pointer). THE CONTROL'S SHAPE. The report is a 64-line shell over YCL_FM_FI_COMPARE_BL. Its selection screen offers three views and the middle one is the point: C_DIFF_DATABASE (differences in the data), C_DIFF_BR (differences CAUSED BY THE BUDGET RATE) and C_NO_RESTRICTION. So the two kinds of difference are separated by design, not by analysis. THE FORMULA, at line 709 of the comparison class: FINAL_DIFF = FKBTR - DMBTR - ZZAMOUNTBRDIFF. FM minus FI, MINUS the part attributable to the budget rate. What remains is the genuine break. The budget-rate difference is EXPECTED and netted out, which is what makes the control usable: a controller looking at FINAL_DIFF is looking at what the rate does not explain. AND THE BASELINE IS NOT ONE THING. GET_BR_IMPACT computes ZZAMOUNTBRLC — the amount at the standard rate — by FOUR different routes depending on the value type. (1) WRTTP '54', actuals: take BSEG-DMBTR directly, sign-corrected by SHKZG ('H' multiplies by -1), either passed in or re-read from BSEG on the document key. (2) WRTTP '51' with VRGNG 'RMBE' and BTART '0200', a purchase-order REDUCTION: fetch the GOODS RECEIPT amount from EKBE through YCL_MM_PO_UTILITIES=>GET_EKBE_AMOUNTS_1 with VGABE '1', then multiply by -1 because it is a reduction. (3) otherwise, if the document carries its own rate KURSF: apply it, honouring SAP's indirect-quotation convention — a NEGATIVE KURSF means divide rather than multiply. (4) otherwise: CONVERT_TO_LOCAL_CURRENCY to USD with TYPE_OF_RATE 'M', and the comment on that branch names it: 'Convert Transaction Amount to UNORE' — the UN Operational Rate of Exchange. SO THE STANDARD SIDE OF THE COMPARISON IS THE UN OPERATIONAL RATE, and that is why the FI rates measured across 2025-2026 move between 1.02041 and 1.17233 while FM holds 1.09529. THE FLAG HAS TWO STATES AND BOTH ARE AGGREGATED SEPARATELY. ZZBRIMPACTED is 'E' when the transaction amount is ZERO — no rate can be derived — and 'X' otherwise. The report calls EXTRACT_GLOBAL_AMOUNT once for each, so a line that cannot be evaluated is reported apart rather than silently counted as zero impact. WHAT THIS DOES TO MY OWN MEASUREMENT. The -1,223,730.83 USD figure compared FKBTR against DMBTR, which is exactly route (1) — correct for WRTTP '54' actuals and NOT correct for purchase-order reductions or for lines carrying their own KURSF. The figure therefore holds for the actuals population and needs the other three routes to cover the rest. The organisation already implements all four.

evidence_for.cite: report 64 lines, radio buttons C_DIFF_DATABASE / C_DIFF_BR / C_NO_RESTRICTION; comparison class line 709 FINAL_DIFF = FKBTR - DMBTR - ZZAMOUNTBRDIFF; GET_BR_IMPACT lines 432-500 with four baseline routes and TYPE_OF_RATE 'M' commented 'Convert Transaction Amount to UNORE'

claim: THE BUDGET-RATE IMPACT ACROSS ALL ROUTES: MINUS 2.37 MILLION USD OVER 11,179 LINES (s098, ALGORITHM A14, replicating GET_BR_IMPACT). THE NUMBER, by year and by baseline route: 2024 route 1 (BSEG-DMBTR) 465 lines, FM 1,156,204.73 against standard 1,156,204.73 — impact EXACTLY ZERO; 2024 route 4 (rate type M) 275 lines, FM 14,672,546.28 against 14,509,827.85 — impact PLUS 162,718.43; 2025 route 1, 7,065 lines, impact -430,752.83; 2025 route 4, 2,131 lines, impact -1,162,024.67; 2026 route 1, 850 lines, impact -300,512.85; 2026 route 4, 393 lines, impact -635,116.52. TOTAL: FM 92,075,779.06 against standard 94,441,467.50, impact -2,365,688.44 USD. THE STRUCTURAL POINT: ONE ROUTE HOLDS THE LINES AND ANOTHER HOLDS THE MONEY. Route 1, the WRTTP '54' actuals, is 8,825 of the 11,684 perimeter lines but only 22.4M USD. Route 4, WRTTP '66' and '57' resolved at the UN operational rate, is 2,859 lines and 73.6M USD. My earlier figure of -1,223,730.83 used route 1 alone and therefore understated the impact by roughly half. TWO YEARS BEHAVE DIFFERENTLY AND BOTH ARE REAL. In 2024 the route-1 impact is exactly zero, because those FI lines carry the SAME EURX rate as FM — nothing to explain. And 2024's route-4 impact is POSITIVE while 2025 and 2026 are negative, because the UN operational rate crossed the fixed rate between those periods. WHAT IS NOT EVALUATED, reported rather than counted as zero: 445 lines whose FI counterpart could not be resolved and 60 with no posting date, out of 11,684. Route 2 — the EKBE goods-receipt baseline for purchase-order reductions — has NO population in this perimeter, so it is implemented in structure and untested against data. AND KURSF IS NOT THE PATH. The class has a branch for the document's own rate, but the comparison is done on AMOUNTS, not on rates: ZZAMOUNTBRDIFF is FKBTR minus the same base valued at the standard rate, which is why route 1 reads DMBTR directly instead of deriving a rate from it.

WHY IT LOOKED EMPTY, and it is worth stating because the shape recurs. GET_BR_IMPACT's second baseline fires on WRTTP '51' with VRGNG 'RMBE' and BTART '0200' — a purchase-order reduction. I searched fmifiit_full and found zero, and reported no population. THE FULL FIGURE ACROSS ALL ROUTES: FM 111,958,704.40 against standard 116,137,203.97 — impact -4,178,499.57 USD over 11,179 actual lines and 4,363 purchase-order items. claim: THE BUDGET RATE FIRES AT TWELVE DISTINCT MOMENTS, AND EACH ONE APPLIES A DIFFERENT PERIMETER (s098, the twelve ZFIX enhancement sources extracted from P01 at last). HOW THEY WERE FINALLY READ. An ENHO has no program of its own; its source lives in a GENERATED INCLUDE named <ENHNAME> padded to 30 characters with '=' and closed with 'E'. ENHOBJ gives the hooked object and ENHINCINX gives the include name. With the right name, RPY_PROGRAM_READ reads it like any other program. All twelve came out — 1,154 lines. EXT-ENHO-SOURCE had stood open because the extractor skipped ENHO as unreadable; it was readable all along, under a name nobody had constructed. THE TWELVE MOMENTS, in lifecycle order: a COMMITMENT LINE is created (SAPLFMOI) · AVAILABILITY IS CHECKED (SAPLFMFC, FM_FUNDS_CHECK_FI and _OI) · a FUND IS RESERVED (FMR3, FMR3_FILL_KBFM_FROM_KBLX) · a FUND IS BLOCKED (SAPLFMFR) · EARMARKED FUNDS ARE REDUCED (CL_FM_EF_POSITION) · earmarked funds are CONSISTENCY-CHECKED (CL_FM_EF_POSITION) · the PAYMENT COMMITMENT is written (SAPLFMR_AD2) · an FI POSTING REACHES FM (SAPLFMRI) · a PBC POSITION is updated (CL_HRFPM_CD_PBC_UPDATE) · an EMPLOYEE EXPENSE is posted (BAPI_ACC_EMPLOYEE_EXP_POST) · COMMITMENTS ARE REVALUED (LFMOIF0M, LFMOIF1C) · RESERVED FUNDS ARE REVALUED (RFFMBW00). THE AVAILABILITY CHECK IS THE ONE THAT CHANGES THE MEANING. The rate is applied INSIDE FM_FUNDS_CHECK, before availability is decided — so the fixed rate is what the budget check sees. This is not a reporting adjustment applied afterwards; it changes what is allowed to post. AND NO TWO CALL SITES PASS THE SAME CONDITIONS. Seven of the eight are passed at the AVC, FI and new-item moments; six at fund reservation, fund block and earmarked-funds reduction (FIKRS derived from the company code in the last of these); and at REVALUATION — both of them — ONLY THE FUND TYPE IS PASSED. Since an unpassed parameter skips its check, revaluation carries NO currency restriction, NO business area, NO commitment item and NO business transaction. The EUR-only limit that shapes every other moment does not apply there. That is the widest gate in the solution and it is invisible from the class alone. THE STAFF PATH IS A SEPARATE MECHANISM. PBC position update and employee expense posting do not use the main perimeter: they gate through YCL_FM_BR_PBC_POSTING_BL and YCL_FM_BR_PAYROLL_POSTING_BL on the PERSONNEL NUMBER, and convert through a second method, CONVERT_TO_CURRENCY_2. ONE SMALL THING WORTH KEEPING: in the staff branch of the payment-commitment enhancement, IV_FIPEX is COMMENTED OUT — so the commitment-item exclusion of GAINS and REVENUE is deliberately not applied at that point.

claim: THE FIXED RATE IS AN OPERATIONAL RATE, FROZEN — AND THAT EXPLAINS 2024 AND CORRECTS MY OWN READING OF IT (s098, AN-BR-2024-FI-AT-EURX). WHAT EURX ACTUALLY IS. 1.09529 is not an arbitrary constant. The UN operational rate for EUR/USD stood at exactly -0.91300 — implicit 1.09529 — from 2024-01-15. EURX was set to the operational rate in force at the START OF THE BIENNIUM and then held. The fixed rate is a SNAPSHOT of the moving one, which is why the two coincide at the beginning and diverge after. AND THE OPERATIONAL RATE CROSSED IT AGAIN. Through 2024 the rate moved 1.09529 (15 Jan), 1.08460, 1.07181, 1.08342, 1.09409, 1.08225, ... and came back to exactly 1.09529 on 15 AUGUST 2024, then went above it — 1.10865, 1.11857 — before falling away through 2025 to 1.04167 and 1.02041. SO THE 2024 'BUDGET RATE' LINES ARE MOSTLY COINCIDENCE, NOT CONVERSION. My filter selected FM lines whose FKBTR/TRBTR equals the EURX rate. In 2024 that catches lines where the OPERATIONAL rate simply WAS 1.09529 that day, so FI posted at it and FM inherited it unchanged. The evidence is decisive: across all 465 route-1 pairs in 2024 the impact is EXACTLY 0.00 — FM equals FI to the cent. A real conversion cannot produce an exact zero against a moving baseline; identical amounts mean no conversion took place. And the posting dates cluster where the rates met: 130 in January and 116 in August. THIS CORRECTS CLAIM 439, which read the 7.6% of 2024 perimeter lines at the EURX rate as the mechanism running partially in its first year. On route 1 it did not run: those lines are rate coincidence. The mechanism reaching 94.7% in 2025 and 97.1% in 2026 stands, because there the operational rate is nowhere near 1.09529 and the match can only come from conversion. THE METHOD LESSON, and it is the same shape as the EURX discovery itself: MATCHING A RATE IS NOT PROOF OF A MECHANISM when the baseline can take that value on its own. The test only separates the two when the fixed and moving rates differ — which is exactly when the impact is non-zero. An impact of exactly zero is not a small effect; it is the signature of no effect at all. ONE RESIDUAL, stated rather than smoothed: 70 of the zero-impact pairs post in February and 85 in September, when the operational rate was 1.08460 and 1.10865. Those need the TRANSLATION DATE (WWERT), which the golden's bkpf extract does not carry, before the coincidence explanation covers them too.

evidence_for.ref: tcurr KURST='M' EUR/USD x bkpf x fmifiit_full
evidence_for.cite: M EUR->USD = -0.91300 (implicit 1.09529) from 2024-01-15 and again from 2024-08-15; EURX = 1.09529 from 2024-01-01; 2024 route-1 impact exactly 0.00 over 465 pairs; posting dates 130 in January, 116 in August

resolution_notes: AN-BR-2024-FI-AT-EURX closed. The answer turned out to be about what EURX IS — a frozen operational rate — rather than about 2024 being anomalous.

claim: THE IMPACT IS ONLY MEASURABLE ON FINANCIAL POSTINGS — COMMITMENTS HAVE NO COMPARISON BASE (s098, user correction, and it withdraws a figure I published). THE CORRECTION: SAP calculates and RECALCULATES commitments through its own complex logic — a commitment is reduced, revalued, carried forward and re-derived as the document behind it changes. There is no stable counterpart amount to difference it against, so a budget-rate IMPACT cannot be computed on the commitment side at all. WHAT THIS WITHDRAWS. Claim 444 reported an impact of -4,178,499.57 USD across all routes, of which -1,812,811.13 came from route 2 — the purchase-order reductions in FMIOI, compared against goods receipts in EKBE. That comparison is not valid. EKBE holds what was received; it is not the standard-rate valuation of the commitment, and the commitment itself is a moving figure. The route-2 number is withdrawn. WHAT STANDS: THE FINANCIAL POSTINGS. fmifiit_full is the FM ACTUAL line-item table and every line in it has an FI counterpart to difference against — that is the whole basis of the organisation's own control, FINAL_DIFF = FKBTR - DMBTR - ZZAMOUNTBRDIFF. On that population, routes 1 and 4 together: FM 92,075,779.06 against standard 94,441,467.50, IMPACT -2,365,688.44 USD over 11,179 lines. That is the defensible figure. WHAT THE COMMITMENT WORK IS STILL WORTH, because it is not wasted. The twelve moments show the budget rate firing on commitments at six of them — new item, availability check, fund reservation, fund block, earmarked-funds reduction and payment commitment. So the rate DOES apply there and it DOES change what the availability check sees. What cannot be done is quantify a difference, because there is nothing stable to difference against. Presence is measurable; impact is not. AND THE FMIOI RE-PULL KEEPS ITS VALUE INDEPENDENTLY: the golden held 13 of 69 columns, without VRGNG, BTART or TWAER, so no commitment question of any kind was answerable before.

evidence_for.cite: the control differences FKBTR against DMBTR — an FI amount — which exists only for actual line items; commitments in FMIOI have no such counterpart

resolution_notes: USER: we only measure impact on financial postings; for commitments SAP has a very complex way of calculating and recalculating them, so there is nothing to compare against. Correct, and it withdraws the route-2 arithmetic.

claim: THE 2024 RESIDUAL IS GONE: IT WAS THE TRANSLATION DATE ALL ALONG (s098, EXT-BKPF-WWERT). bkpf in the golden held 18 of the table's 122 columns and did not carry WWERT — the TRANSLATION DATE, which is the date SAP converts on when it is set, in preference to the posting date. Re-pulled with all fields, 1,939,003 rows over 122 columns. THE RESULT IS DECISIVE. Of the 422 resolvable 2024 pairs whose FM ratio equals the EURX rate, 416 match the UN OPERATIONAL RATE IN FORCE ON THEIR TRANSLATION DATE. Not their posting date — every single one of the 422 carries a WWERT distinct enough to matter, and the February and September clusters that looked unexplained were documents translated on an earlier date when the operational rate was 1.09529. THE REMAINING SIX CARRY AN EXPLICIT DOCUMENT RATE. KURSF is set on them: 0.91300- on two (which is exactly 1/1.09529 — the EURX value entered by hand), 0.92200-, 0.93300- and 0.90200- on the others, each matching the operational rate of its own translation date. So all 422 are accounted for by the standard machinery. THIS COMPLETES THE CORRECTION. The 2024 lines matching the EURX rate are NOT budget-rate conversions. They are documents whose ordinary conversion happened to land on 1.09529, because EURX is itself the operational rate frozen at the start of the biennium. The measured impact of exactly 0.00 across those pairs was telling the truth: nothing was converted. AND A SMALL DATA-QUALITY FINDING FELL OUT: two documents, 4500000113 and 4500000114, carry WWERT = 22040723 — a translation date in the year 2204. The rate they actually used is the one on their KURSF, so the posting is right and the date is a typo; but any report that derives a rate from WWERT would take the last rate in the table for them.

evidence_for.cite: bkpf re-pulled 1,939,003 rows / 122 columns (was 18); of 422 resolvable 2024 pairs, 416 match the operational rate on their WWERT; the other 6 carry an explicit KURSF, two of them 0.91300- = 1/1.09529; documents 4500000113/114 carry WWERT=22040723

claim: THE BUDGET RATE IS TWO MECHANISMS, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS IN THE ENHANCEMENTS (s098, user correction on the framing). IT SPLITS INTO NON-PERSONNEL AND PERSONNEL. Everything measured so far — the eight-dimension perimeter, the twelve moments, the EURX rate, the -2,365,688.44 USD impact — is the NON-PERSONNEL side. The PERSONNEL side is computed in HR, INSIDE THE PAYROLL SCHEMA, which is a different mechanism entirely and is not visible in any of the enhancement sources. MEASURED, BY WHICH CLASS EACH ENHANCEMENT INSTANTIATES: EIGHT are exclusively non-personnel, using only YCL_FM_BR_EXCHANGE_RATE_BL — BR_REVALUATION, BR_REVAL_RESFUND, EF_FUND_RESERVATION, EXCHANGERATE_CHECK_CONS, _FUNDBLOCK, _KBLEW, _NEW_ITEM and _PAYCOMMIT. THREE ARE DUAL, instantiating a personnel class as well: EXCHANGERATE_AVC and _FI both reach for YCL_FM_BR_PAYROLL_POSTING_BL on their staff branch, and _PBC_POS_UPD reaches for YCL_FM_BR_PBC_POSTING_BL. ONE IS EXCLUSIVELY PERSONNEL: BR_BAPI_EMPLOYEE_POST, which does nothing but instantiate the payroll class. THE USER STATES THE NON-PERSONNEL SIDE IS NINE ENHANCEMENTS PLUS THE REPORT. The measurement gives eight EXCLUSIVELY non-personnel and three dual, so the ninth is one of the dual ones counted by its main path — most likely EXCHANGERATE_FI or _AVC, whose primary branch is non-personnel and whose staff branch is secondary. Recorded as measured rather than forced to the stated count. AND THE CONTROL PROGRAM IS CONFIRMED: transaction YFM_FI_BR_COMP runs YFM_FI_COMPARE_INCLUDING_BR — the program already read and analysed. TSTC resolves it. So the GL-difference control that was analysed is the right one, reached by a transaction code rather than by its program name. WHAT IS NOW KNOWN TO BE MISSING: the payroll-schema side. It is calculated in the HR schema, not in ABAP enhancements, so none of the extraction done so far can reach it.

resolution_notes: USER: the budget rate splits into non-personnel — the enhancements plus the report — and personnel, calculated in the HR payroll schema; and the GL control is transaction YFM_FI_BR_COMP.

claim: THE PERSONNEL SIDE OF THE BUDGET RATE IS GATED BY AN HR FEATURE, AND ITS TWO-STEP CONVERSION IS DEAD CODE (s098, AN-BR-PERSONNEL-PAYROLL-SCHEMA, first pass). THE GATE IS NOT A PERIMETER — IT IS A DECISION TREE. YCL_FM_BR_PBC_POSTING_BL:: CHECK_CONDITIONS reads PA0001, the employee's organisational assignment valid on the position's DUE_DATE, moves it into a PC205 structure and calls CL_HRPA_FEATURE=>GET_VALUE( FEATURE = 'YYCDR' ). The personnel number is in scope only if the feature returns 'Y'. So where the non-personnel side has eight declared ranges, the personnel side has ONE HR FEATURE — a decision tree maintained in PE03, evaluated per employee per date. The two mechanisms do not share a perimeter, a gate or a maintenance path. THE TWO-STEP CONVERSION EXISTS AND IS DISABLED. CONVERT_TO_BUDGET_RATE performs a round trip: the amount is converted to EUR at rate type M — the operational rate — and the EUR result is then converted to USD at rate type EURX. That is the personnel equivalent of the fixed-rate valuation. BOTH CALLS TO IT SIT INSIDE `IF 1 = 2.` in ZFIX_EXCHANGERATE_PBC_POS_UPD. Deliberately switched off, left in place, never removed. WHAT RUNS INSTEAD is CONVERT_TO_CURRENCY_2 on the non-personnel class, and it runs only under `IF CS_POS-WAERS = 'USD'`. The code comments why: 'ALL PBC Documents are in USD. Even if postings are in EUR.' So the payroll-commitment side converts USD to USD through the second conversion method rather than through its own budget-rate method. AND THE TRACE IS EMPTY, WHICH IS CONSISTENT. The path ends by calling Y_FM_UPDATE_BR_FM_POS IN UPDATE TASK to record the before-and-after amounts in YTFM_BR_FM_POS. That table was extracted this session and holds ZERO ROWS. Either the guarded branch is not being reached or the update is not landing — the two facts agree and neither has been separated from the other yet. WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE IMPACT FIGURE. The -2,365,688.44 USD measured on financial postings is the NON-PERSONNEL side only, and now for a second reason: not merely that the personnel calculation lives in the payroll schema, but that the FM-side personnel path is largely switched off. Staff cost is the organisation's largest spend category and its budget-rate treatment remains unmeasured. STILL NOT REACHED: the payroll schema itself. The feature YYCDR decides WHO is in scope; the schema decides WHAT is computed, and a schema is not ABAP source.

evidence_for.cite: CHECK_CONDITIONS reads PA0001 and calls CL_HRPA_FEATURE=>GET_VALUE(FEATURE='YYCDR'), CHECK LV_BR='Y'; CONVERT_TO_BUDGET_RATE does M to EUR then EURX to USD; both call sites are inside IF 1 = 2; what runs is CONVERT_TO_CURRENCY_2 under IF CS_POS-WAERS = 'USD'; YTFM_BR_FM_POS holds 0 rows

claim: THE PERSONNEL BUDGET-RATE PERIMETER IS 2,086 EMPLOYEES — 8.8% OF THE WORKFORCE, AND ALMOST ALL OF THEM IN PARIS (s098, AN-BR-YYCDR-FEATURE). HOW THE PERIMETER WAS READ. Feature YYCDR is a decision tree, not a range, and T549B held nothing for it — but T549D records that SAP COMPILES every feature into a generated program, here /1PAPA/FEAT350YYCDR over structure PC205. That program reads like any other through RPY_PROGRAM_READ: 118 lines of nested CASE. A decision tree maintained in PE03 is therefore fully readable, which is worth knowing because nothing about it is visible in a table search. THE TREE IS THREE LEVELS: employee group (PERSG), then business area (GSBER), then personnel area (WERKS). Business area must be GEF throughout — every other value returns blank. AND THE EMPLOYEE GROUP CHANGES WHICH COUNTRIES QUALIFY, which is the part no summary would have guessed. Groups 1 and 2 return 'Y' for BE00, DE00, FR00, IT00 and NL00 — the five euro-zone personnel areas. Group 3 returns 'Y' for the same list MINUS BELGIUM. Group M returns 'Y' for FRANCE ONLY, with BE00, DE00, IT00 and NL00 explicitly set to blank rather than falling through. So the perimeter is not 'euro-zone staff': it is euro-zone staff with two hand-cut exceptions. THE POPULATION, measured against PA0001 — which had to be extracted, because the golden contained NO HR table at all. Of 23,747 distinct employees with a current org assignment, 2,086 fall in scope: 8.8%. By employee group, 1,234 in group 1, 777 in group 2 and 397 in group M. AND FOUR OF THE FIVE COUNTRIES ARE ALMOST EMPTY. By personnel area the in-scope records are FR00 2,370, IT00 21, BE00 9, DE00 8 — and NL00 ZERO. The tree lists five euro-zone areas and four of them carry a rounding error's worth of staff. The mechanism is, in practice, a Paris mechanism. AND NL00 CANNOT FIRE AT ALL. It is not that the branch is unused — the Netherlands personnel area holds SEVEN current employees and NOT ONE of them carries business area GEF: they sit on PFF (17 records) and MBF (4). The branch is reachable only for a combination that does not exist in the data. The same shape in miniature elsewhere: BE00 has 39 employees of whom 8 carry GEF, DE00 has 90 of whom 8, IT00 has 358 of whom 21. THE BUSINESS AREA DOES THE REAL NARROWING. FR00 holds 13,288 employees in total and only 2,370 in-scope records — so GSBER = GEF, not the country list, is what cuts the population down. The country list is close to decorative for everywhere except France, where it also does very little.
